name: Dipolieia
summary: Zeus Polieus' archaic ox-slaying on the Acropolis — the Bouphonia — when the beast that eats the grain on the altar is struck, the axe is tried for murder, and the city closes the old year with a rite already called ancient in classical Athens.
testimonia: Pausanias 1.24.4 (the ox-slayer at the altar of Zeus Polieus)
Pausanias 1.28.10 (the annual trial of the axe, from the time of Erechtheus)
